significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both the phenomenon that factual consistency varies with retrieval-circuit overlap and the mechanism that a "shared mid-layer storage locus" feeds "format-specific access pathways" whose selective ablation impairs one phrasing while sparing others. This combines a form-(ii) causal decomposition with a form-(iii) predictive coupling—facts with "the least overlapping circuits" should be least behaviorally consistent—and would constrain explanations beyond individual facts by distinguishing access failure from missing storage; that distinction matters to the subject-enrichment and attribute-extraction account developed by Geva et al. (2023) and to the prompt-sensitive recall documented by Jiang et al. (2020) and Elazar et al. (2021). True and false outcomes are distinguishable: selective effects plus the overlap-consistency relation support the account, whereas shared circuits or no relation would rule out this proposed general explanation, although not every possible access-based account. The topic-substitution check lowers the assessment from the very top: prompt-dependent retrieval is already suggested by the assigned topic, but the shared-storage/split-access decomposition and quantitative overlap law are specific additions false of the median claim.

reach.justification: The principal reusable handle is the "circuit-overlap (Jaccard)" score, supplemented by identified "format-specific" heads as ablation or potential strengthening targets. It is mainly post hoc because circuits must be extracted across phrasings after the model's recall behavior is available, so it does not clearly forecast failures with an independent action window; its likely users are mechanistic-interpretability and factual-reliability researchers rather than deployers directly. After per-model re-extraction, the hypothesized inverse overlap-consistency relation would still predict what should be found, but the claim asserts coverage across query formats rather than architectures or training regimes and explicitly allows that results "may not generalize across relations." The topic-substitution check supports only moderate reach: the named metric and transferable relation add more than the broad topic alone, but deleting them leaves no concrete diagnostic or intervention and therefore would merit below 5.
